author: resilience-lead (AI practice-lead agent). Expected outcomes written on 27 Oct 2026, before any engine run. Advises; the product owner approves (gate RQ1).
note: Five reference scenarios (owner decision D13). Each takes its shape from public material: an enforcement notice, a regulator statement, a provider incident report or regulator guidance. Answers that the public material does not state are scenario assumptions, listed per scenario. The scenarios are illustrative clients, never the named firms: no statement here describes the named firm's current controls. Expected outcomes follow the rules in DESIGN.md sections 4 to 9 and decision-matrix.json. The posture number is calibrated in RQ5 and is not predicted; the exposure level and the rating cap are.
conventions: Answer values are the v2 option labels in DESIGN.md section 12.
Facts use the Sovereign IQ fact ids (ent.flags, org.establishments, org.sector) plus ent.res_flags for REG-02.

Obligation status rule (DESIGN.md 7.3): all asked checks meet and none unasked = met; no asked check meets or partly meets = not_evidenced; otherwise partly; nothing asked = not_assessed. Unknown counts as a failed check.
Proven-versus-tolerance comparison: proven band lower than the tolerance band = meets; same band = partly; higher band or 'Not proven' = fails.

Impact = cost per hour (client input, low-high) x hours between proven recovery time (AF-DR-01) and required RTO (EX-03); gap low = max(0, proven lower bound - RTO upper bound), gap high = proven upper bound - RTO lower bound.
Exposure: 3 or more Critical = Severe (rating at most Fragile); 1 or more Critical, or 4 or more High = High (rating at most Managed); 1 or more High = Moderate; otherwise Low.

scenarios.name: UK retail bank under PRA SS1/21 and FCA SYSC 15A, after a failed platform migration run by a critical IT supplier (workshop mode)
scenarios.summary: Shape from the FCA and PRA penalty against TSB (20 Dec 2022): an April 2018 migration to a new platform run by a critical third-party supplier failed; branch, telephone, online and mobile banking were disrupted, with some problems until December 2018. Here, a PRA-regulated retail bank whose main digital and branch banking service depends on one supplier's platform. Answers are scenario assumptions consistent with that shape.

scenarios.name: EU insurer under DORA after a mass endpoint failure caused by a security vendor's update, with ransomware exposure (executive mode)
scenarios.summary: Shape from the 18-19 Jul 2024 CrowdStrike content update that Microsoft estimated affected 8.5 million Windows devices, and from ENISA's 2025 threat landscape (ransomware the most impactful threat). An EU insurer's claims processing service: workplace devices and servers fail together through one security vendor, and backups are recoverable but not immutable. Tests that severe cyber exposure adds controls and findings but never a higher rung (D3).

scenarios.name: Australian superannuation fund under APRA CPS 230 after its cloud provider deleted its private cloud environment (workshop mode)
scenarios.summary: Shape from Google Cloud's incident report (May 2024): a Google Cloud VMware Engine private cloud of one customer (UniSuper) was deleted after a parameter was left blank at deployment; backups in Google Cloud Storage in the same region were not affected and, with third-party backup software, were instrumental in the restoration, which took several days of 24x7 work. Here, an APRA-regulated fund whose member services run on one provider and region. Tests that the ladder correctly gives backup and restore for a relaxed objective while the finding targets the proven recovery time and the shared failure domain.

sources.citation: Google Cloud blog, 'Sharing details on a recent incident impacting one of our customers' (25 May 2024)
sources.usedFor: Shape only: provider-side deletion of a whole private cloud; same-region backups survived; recovery over several days. The proven recovery time '>24 hours' is a scenario assumption drawn from 'several days'.

scenarios.name: New York state-chartered bank under NYDFS 23 NYCRR 500.16 and the FFIEC BCM booklet, with ransomware exposure (executive mode)
scenarios.summary: Shape from the NYDFS ransomware guidance (30 Jun 2021): 74 ransomware attacks reported by DFS-regulated companies from Jan 2020 to May 2021; DFS expects segregated, offline backups and restore tests. Here, a NY state-chartered, federally supervised bank whose backups are immutable but whose restore has not been tested and whose recovery could be reached by an attacker.

scenarios.name: Singapore payments firm under the MAS BCM Guidelines, on-premises with one hyperscaler and a sovereign provider, after a primary data-centre failure (workshop mode)
scenarios.summary: Shape from MAS's statement on the 14 Oct 2023 outage at DBS and Citibank: the primary data centres failed, both banks activated their backup data centres but could not fully recover within the required timeframe; MAS requires critical systems to be restorable within four hours. Here, a MAS-licensed payments firm whose payment service runs in a colocation data centre, with recovery to a second site, a hyperscaler and a local sovereign provider. Tests the MAS TRM four-hour floor (recorded, no change), the three-yearly BCM audit and a sovereign provider in the playbook.
